System Map

Read together, the four themes are not separate pressures. Three loops connect them. Flooding builds the case (B1): rising flood risk makes the case for public money, which lets the plan hold the line. Insurers demand storm readiness (B2): storm damage tightens insurance terms, which push the club to invest before the next loss. What members can pay (B3): if public money does not come, the club’s own defences draw on members, and members set the limit. Warmer seas sit beside them, lengthening the season and worsening the water at the same time. Arrows that cross a colour are connections no single theme carries.

LoopNameWhat it doesThis cycle
B1Flooding builds the case
The shoreline plan		Rising flood risk builds the case for public money, the money lets the plan hold the line, and holding the line reduces flooding.Priming: plans refreshed, no money committed
B2Insurers demand storm readiness
Storms		Storm damage tightens insurers' terms, tighter terms push the club to invest in its haven, and investment reduces damage.Turning: storm plans a condition of cover
B3What members can pay
The shoreline plan		Spending on the club's own defences draws on members' fees and reserves, and what members can pay limits that spending.Priming: no defence spending yet

Hover over a status for its meaning: Priming means the parts are in place but the circle has not yet closed at scale. Turning means every step in the loop has current evidence, so it is running now.

The Scenario Matrix’s horizontal axis asks which loop pays for the waterfront: loop B1 (flooding builds the case), if public money follows the case, or loop B3 (what members can pay), if it does not. Its vertical axis asks whether loop B1 can keep pace with the outside switch, global emissions, that is whether the frontage is held in place or moved back.

What it means: the club cannot slow the rise or the storms, but it can decide whether it is inside loop B1 when the plan is refreshed, keep loop B2 working in its favour, and build high enough that loop B3 never has to carry the whole cost.
